text:
alex: heads up — canary perf alert on 6e12c8b (merged from PR #4123). p95 decode latency up ~34ms on short prompts. CI perf run: https://ci/redwood/runs/1801034000 :eyes:
perf-ci-bot: regression detected: p95 +34ms vs baseline (main @ 6e12c8b) — marking as rollout blocker
deploy-bot: rollout paused automatically for canary group "prod-eu" — manual review required

maria: ok i'm grabbing a local repro. quick run with small prompt (len 32) shows decode step spike in flamegraph, looks like extra memcpy in attention backend
maria: paste: ```
# flamegraph snippet (call stack top -> bottom)
runtime::decode_step
fused_ops::dispatch_kernel
kernelselector::choose_attention
gpu_kernels::attn_blocked_memcpy
memcopy_kernel
```

sam: interesting — PR #4123 touched fused-op selection heuristics and batching thresholds. did anybody run perf tests for short sequences?

alex: looks like not enough coverage on short-seq latency in the smoke suite. CI perf only ran long prompt tests in that job. my bad on the gap.

irene: ran a quick bisect across main..6e12c8b. suspect commit 9f3a2b4 changed selection: `if (seq_len > 24) use_fused = true` (previously 32).

maria: confirmed locally: reverting that single line brings p95 back within 3ms of baseline. quick diff: ```diff
- if (seq_len > 24) use_fused = true;
+ if (seq_len > 32) use_fused = true; // revert heuristic
```

sam: why would lowering threshold cause memcpy cost increase? maybe fused kernel uses a path that forces KV cache reshuffle for small batches?

maria: looked at KV cache traces — we see extra cache invalidations on prefix alignment when fused kernel runs for short seqs. Eviction pattern changes and triggers extra host<->device copies.

alex: timeline: PR #4123 aimed to prefer fused kernels earlier to win throughput. but side-effect is KV layout mismatch for short decode paths.

irene: CI notes: perf job 1801034000 shows regression on multiple machines (A100, H100), consistent. I started a bisect run against infra/perf-branch to be sure.

perf-ci-bot: bisect finished — culprit commit 9f3a2b4 (author: sam) changed kernel selection heuristic.

sam: oof — that's my commit. I can open a hotfix PR to restore previous threshold and add a unit perf test for short sequences + KV invariants.

maria: can you also add a KV cache integration test that simulates prefix reuse across fused/non-fused transitions? that'll catch layout regressions.

sam: yup. patch ready in my branch: https://git/redwood/pulls/4189 — includes revert + new perf test. local perf: p95 delta now +2ms vs baseline.

alex: great. can we get a quick canary patch deploy? deploy-bot: if we merge, will it unblock automatically?

deploy-bot: manual approval required for hotfix canary. automated canary rollback policy will still be in effect.

irene: i'll approve once we have CI green on the new perf job (short-seq job added). queued run: https://ci/redwood/runs/1801034550

perf-ci-bot: short-seq perf job passed for PR 4189: p95 within +3ms of baseline. baseline comparison artifacts: https://artifacts/redwood/1801034550

alex: approved and merging now. rolling hotfix to prod-eu canary. please monitor dashboards.
maria: watching memory/KV eviction metrics. initial canary looks good — p95 back to normal on the dashboard. :thumbsup:

sam: i'm following up with a follow-on to make kernel selector explicitly query KV cache compatibility before choosing fused path. won't assume layout equivalence.

alex: thanks everyone. action items: sam -> follow-up selector guard; maria -> KV integration tests merged to perf suite; irene -> add short-seq perf to pre-merge checks. I'll file a retro note.

irene: filing retro now: https://docs/redwood/retro/1801034567-regression

alex: marking thread resolved when rollout fully completes. thanks for the quick response team. :rocket:
